narration: Your app can have login and still expose the wrong user’s data. Authentication and data access are not the same thing.
onScreenText: Logged in ≠ allowed to see everything.
voiceDirection: Clear and direct. Emphasize the contrast.

narration: Imagine two users, Alice and Bob, and one profiles table containing one row for each of them.
Without a row-level policy, a request can return rows the current user should never see if your access rules are missing or incorrect.
onScreenText: No row policy → too much data.
captionText: The database returns more than intended.

narration: Row Level Security moves that access rule into the database. The database checks the current identity before allowing a row to be read or changed.
Alice asks for profiles. The policy compares the row owner with Alice’s user ID, so Alice’s row passes and Bob’s row is filtered out.
voiceDirection: Very visual and easy to follow.

narration: Bob makes the same request and gets the opposite result. The query can look identical, while the database returns different rows for each identity.
voiceDirection: Emphasize same query and different result.

narration: Authentication proves who the user is. Authorization decides what that user is allowed to access. Row Level Security is one place those data rules can be enforced.
Before shipping a Supabase app, review the policies on every table your client can reach. Login protects identity. Policies protect which data each identity can actually use.
captionText: Login protects identity. Policies protect data access.
